Hi Sam —

Great talking earlier today. Short recap and proposed next steps so we can make progress on the evaluation: 

Key points from discovery:
- Primary workload: user-facing document search + concise summarization and classification for legal docs (~3-7 pages per doc).
- Latency target: p50 < 300ms for short answer path; p95 service-level target to be discussed.
- Quality metrics you care about: factuality on extraction tasks, precision on classification (entailment/categorical labels).
- Data constraints: some records contain PII/PHI; you prefer minimal data sharing and redaction before upload.
- Deployment preference: start hosted sandbox, then evaluate Redwood Dedicated for predictable throughput.

Model recommendations (initial):
- redwood-alpha-4-8k (balanced accuracy + latency for extractive QA) — start here for baseline benchmarking.
- redwood-fast-8k-quant (low-latency, quantized variant) — good for tight latency budgets; expect slight quality tradeoff on edge cases.
- llama-3-13b-q4 (cost-efficient alternative) — consider if cost per inference is the primary constraint.

Benchmarks & evaluation kit:
- We host a small benchmark suite and example eval configs here: https://redwood.ai/benchmarks/overview?suite=production-inference
- Attached is a prompt/sample template you can use to upload representative prompts and expected outputs.

Ask: to run a meaningful model-fit eval we need a representative prompt set (50–100 prompts is ideal) plus 10–20 explicit edge cases where models have historically failed (ambiguous references, long context with repeated entities, redaction-sensitive fields). Please include:
  - The raw prompt (or redacted version)
  - The expected/desired output (if available)
  - A short note if the prompt contains PII/PHI and how you recommend redacting (or whether we should use a tokenized placeholder)

Redaction guidance (recommended):
- Replace any direct identifiers with bracketed placeholders: e.g., [PERSON_NAME], [ACCOUNT_NUMBER], [SSN], [CASE_ID].
- For free-text PHI, replace exact tokens with [REDACTED_PHRASE].
- Keep surrounding context intact so we can evaluate model behavior on confusability without keeping sensitive tokens.
- If you can supply a hashed ID mapping (one-way hash) that preserves uniqueness but removes the raw value, that works for entity-level tests.

Upload options & security:
- Preferred: upload redacted prompt CSV to the Drive folder we created (link below) or to a secure pre-signed S3 link we'll provide.
- We can also accept fully redacted samples; if you'd rather keep raw data on-prem, we can run a remote evaluation with an engineer present (requires a short SOW).

Timeline / next steps:
1) If you agree: share sample prompts + edge cases by EOD 2027-06-28.
2) We'll run a 1-week model-fit sweep across the three model choices and return a short report with per-model precision/recall and latency numbers.
3) Quick sync to review results and decide on Dedicated pilot.

Attachments: [Attachment: prompt_samples_template.csv (CSV)]
Related links: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-example-upload

If you want, I can loop in Marissa (CS) to stand up a secure upload flow; Ben can scope a minimal SOW if you prefer an engineer-assisted eval.

Thanks,
Rachel

Sam —

Answers below and added a couple of notes on secure upload.

1) SOC 2: Redwood has an ISO/SOC2 Type II report. I can share the SOC2 summary and our security whitepaper with your security team. For full report access we typically sign an NDA/secure access agreement — happy to start that process if your security team needs it.

2) Retention: For prompt samples submitted for model-fit, our default is to keep them for 30 days post-eval and then delete them unless you request longer retention. If you supply already-redacted prompts, we will mark them accordingly and can delete them immediately after the run if you prefer.

3) NDA / Data Processing: For any non-redacted data we ask for a short DPA and a scoping addendum. For redacted or synthetic data we can proceed without additional paperwork.

I've attached a short eval playbook and included the secure upload options. We can provide a pre-signed S3 link (time-limited) for uploads or you can drop files into the Drive folder we've shared.
